title: Advertisement for the 3rd Call for proposals under BioNEST-PU
text:
KEY LINES:


FULL TEXT:

BioNEST- Panjab University (BNPU)
Invites applications for “3rd Call for Proposals” under
Sustainable Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Fund (SEED Fund) scheme
funded by BIRAC, New Delhi
BioNEST- Panjab University (BNPU) – as a BIRAC SEED fund partner provides capital
assistance to the tune of up to ₹30 Lakh to strengthen start-ups with new and meritorious ideas,
innovations and technologies for bio-incubation in the region over a period of twenty-four
months (w.e.f. the date of the start of the project i.e., signing of “Seed Fund Implementation
Agreement” which would not be more than 8-10 weeks from the date of sanction). The BIRAC
SEED Fund support to start-ups is to act as a bridge between promoter’s investment and
venture/ angel investment for enabling start-up to attain sustainability in the long run.
The salient features/ terms for the usage of fund support under the BIRAC SEED Fund scheme
are as under:
1) The scheme supports high level innovation in Life Sciences and related areas and supports
post proof‐of‐principle/ prototype/ process optimization/ product validation aimed at
affordable product/ process development addressing societal needs.
2) Seed fund of up to Rs. 30.00 lakhs per start-up – selected on merit, as the early-stage fund
(refundable) against equity support of up to 10% of the paid-up capital of the start-up can
be extended to support product development, process development, innovation and
commercialization.
3) The SEED fund is only for registered start-ups with minimum 51% ownership by Indian
citizens (does not include OCI or PIO) and under BIRAC SEED Fund, a company will be
considered as start-up,
a. Up to 5 years from the date of its incorporation/ registration.
b. It is working towards innovation development, deployment or commercialization of
new products, processes or services driven by technology or intellectual property.
c. If its turnover for any of the financial years has not exceeded Rs. 25 Cr.
4) The seed support shall be open to all eligible applicants regardless of their affiliation with
the BioNEST.
5) Applications shall be considered by a BIRAC SEED Fund ‘Advisory Team Cum Selection
Panel’ with experts in relevant domains.
6) Successful applicants shall enter into a governing agreement with BioNEST-PU which
shall incorporate provisions for “Exit” from the start-up.
➢ The application form is provided on the next page.
Duly filled form may be submitted by 5:30 p.m. till 1st April 2025 by email
(bionestpu@pu.ac.in).
BioNEST, Panjab University, Chandigarh
SEED Fund
APPLICATION FORM
PART A: General Information
1. Company Name and Incorporation Certificate
o Name of the Company
o (Upload Incorporation Certificate along with the application form)
2. Brief Overview of the Company
o A short description of the company, its mission, and the products or services it
provides.
3. Contact Details
a. Address
b. Email
c. Contact Number
4. Management Team
a. Name
b. Education
c. Designation
5. Company Legal Structure
o Type of company
6. Year of Establishment
o Year the company was incorporated.
7. Annual Revenue (if applicable)
o Previous year’s revenue, if applicable.
8. Previous Seed/ Investment Raised (if applicable)
o Details of any previous funding received (amount, investor names, etc.)
PART B: Technology Description
1. Title of the Technology
o The name or title of the technology or innovation.
2. Problem/ Market Opportunity
o Describe the problem you are solving or the opportunity you are creating in
the market.
3. Status of Work Already Carried Out
a. Developmental work done so far:
o Brief details on any research, development, or prototype work carried out to
date.
b. Intellectual Property (IP) Filed (if any):
o Any patents, trademarks, or other IP protection filed for the technology.
4. Details of the Proposed Work to be completed with SEED Support
a. Describe the technology you plan to develop or implement using the SEED support.
b. Duration/Time Schedule:
o A timeline or milestones for the work to be completed.
5. Competitive Landscape
o Describe competitors and existing market solutions.
6. Revenue Model
o How will the company generate revenue? Describe pricing strategy, business
model, etc.
7. Business Plan/ Scale-up Plan
o Key partners (e.g., suppliers, distributors, etc.)
o Any existing customers or market traction
8. Market Size and Target Audience
o Estimated market size for the product/ service
9. Technology Differentiation
o How your technology is different from and superior to existing solutions in the
market.
10. Prototype Details
o If applicable, provide details on the prototype available.
11. Technology Readiness Level (TRL)
o The stage of development according to the Technology Readiness Level
(TRL) scale (1-9).
12. Regulatory Approvals/Certifications
o Any necessary regulatory approvals or certifications required.
PART C: Budget
1. Details of Proposed Budget
o Break down the budget into categories (e.g., R&D, marketing, operations,
equipment, etc.).
2. Funding Requirements Linked to Project Milestones
o Breakdown of funding required at different project milestones (e.g., product
development, marketing launch, etc.).
3. Any Other Financial Requirements
o Any additional financial needs or support required outside of the proposed
budget.
4. Detailed Budget Breakdown
o Specific categories for how the SEED funding will be used.
5. Financial Projections for the Next 2-3 Years
o Expected income, expenses, and projected profitability.
6. Use of Funds
o Specific allocation for R&D, marketing, product development, etc.
7. Potential Financial Risks and Mitigation
o Key risks facing the project and how the company plans to mitigate them.
Part D: Market & Impact Assessment
1. Market Validation
o Any market surveys, pilot programs, or research showing validation of the
product/ technology.
2. Impact Potential
o Social, economic, or environmental impact the technology or solution aims to
achieve.
3. Customer engagement Strategy
o How will you engage/attract customers (e.g., digital marketing, sales strategy,
partnerships, etc.)?
Part E: Risk Assessment
1. Risk Analysis
o Overview of major risks associated with the project (e.g., technical, market,
financial).
2. Mitigation Plan
o How the company plans to mitigate or reduce the impact of these risks.
